SCIENCE ADVENTURE 29 · CLASS 31

Penguin’s Hot and Cold Lab

Age 4–5 YearsClass 31 · ScienceSkill Hot and cold

Soup, ice, cocoa, popsicle — tap HOT or COLD for each one.

Play the science game ↓Print the worksheet ↓Play with a finger, a stylus or a mouse. Instructions are spoken aloud.
PLAY · HOT AND COLD

Penguin’s Hot and Cold Lab

Things can be hot or cold! Look at each picture, then tap HOT or COLD.

A steaming bowl of soup. Hot or cold?

A bowl of ice cubes. Hot or cold?

A mug of cocoa with marshmallows. Hot or cold?

A frosty blue popsicle. Hot or cold?

Temperature expert!

Soup and cocoa are HOT. The ice bowl and popsicle are COLD. Feel the steam — it always means hot!

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

Temperature talk is safety talk: hot things can burn, and steam is the clue. The safe test for children: use your EYES first — steam or ice tells you before a finger does.

Illustration note: Loaded by content: the file named owls-earth-and-sun-discovery actually carries this Penguin’s Hot and Cold Lab artwork (the R2 export shifted files 20–30 by one slot).

Prefer paper? The Penguin’s Hot and Cold Lab worksheet prints the same experiment with room to think and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.
